There are three kinds of l: (1) (mere) l without combining with other consonants. (2) (mixed) l which is the combination of two l-letters- ll. (3) (conjunct) l which becomes conjunct with k, y, etc. Of them, (1) "l" is (a) the "l" that is at the beginning of a word, (b) "l" that is in the middle of a word and (c) "l" that is at the end of a word.
(2) "l" is of two kinds: (a) "ll" that is in the middle of a word, (b) "ll" that is at the end of a word.
(3) "l" is of three kinds: (a) l connect with the preceding consonant, (b) l connected with middle consonant and (c) l connect with the final consonant. Tipi, 18, 1. l letter which is added to form a conjunct/double "ll". Tipi, 18, 1.

 letter "l" included in the roots "la, lā, lī, lū". (1) root "lā" belongs to Bhūvādi group and is in the sense of (a) taking = ādāna, (b) becoming = pavattana.
(၂) root "lī" belongs to Bhūvādigaṇika, curādigaṇika, divādigaṇika, kīyādigaṇika. Of them, Bhūvādigaṇika, curādigaṇika root "lī" is in the sense of becoming liquid and breaking into piece. Kīyādigaṇika root "lī" is in the sense of approaching and Divādigaṇika root "lī" has these two meanings. In Bhūvādigiuṇa, there are verbs formed as layati, layanti; in Curādigiuṇa, lāyati, lāyanti; in Divādigiuṇa, līyati, līyanti; in Kīyādigiuṇa, lināti, līnanti, etc. In all four groups, nouns are formed as Līnaṃ, sallīnaṃ, paṭisallānaṃ, leṇaṃ, layo, palayo, ālayo, etc. (Nīti, dhātu. 254.
